title: Slow-cooker beef goulash
subtitle: Hungarian-style paprika stew, deep red and gently spiced
excerpt: Braising steak in a rich paprika and tomato sauce, cooked slowly until the beef is very tender. A hearty, warming stew that needs only rice or bread alongside.
sourceNotes: Goulash (gulyas) is a Hungarian peasant dish with roots in the 9th century, documented in Karoly Gundel, Hungarian Cookery Book (1934). The slow-cooker adaptation follows the standard braised method common in British cookbooks.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob, adding a splash of water if needed.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe easily. Use a large slow cooker and divide between containers once cooled.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Goulash tastes better the next day. Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Hungarian meat stew seasoned generously with paprika, traditionally made with beef or pork and cooked long and slow until the sauce is thick and the meat is tender.

content.text: is one of the most satisfying stews you can make in a slow cooker. Generous paprika, braising steak, and a tin of tomatoes go in together and emerge, eight hours later, as a thick, brick-red sauce with meat that breaks apart at the touch of a spoon.

The paprika does the heavy lifting here. Use a mix of sweet and smoked if you have both; if you only have sweet, it will still be very good. Brown the beef first for colour and depth, then everything else goes into the slow cooker raw.
Serve with egg noodles, rice, or thick bread to catch the sauce. Soured cream on top at the table is traditional and very good.

Season {{braising-steak}} of braising steak with salt. Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a frying pan over high heat. Brown the beef in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until coloured all over. Transfer to the slow cooker.

Add {{onion}} sliced onions, {{pepper-red}} sliced red peppers, and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic to the slow cooker. Stir in {{paprika-sweet}} of sweet paprika, {{paprika-smoked}} of smoked paprika, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, and {{caraway-seeds}} of caraway seeds if using. Pour over {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes and {{stock-beef}} of beef stock. Tuck in {{bay-leaves}} of bay.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 7 to 8 hours, or HIGH for 4 to 5 hours. The beef should break apart easily when pressed with a spoon. Discard the bay leaves, taste, and adjust seasoning before serving.

rows.symptom: The sauce tastes flat despite lots of paprika
rows.cause: Paprika loses its potency if the jar has been open for a long time, or if it was not bloomed in oil.
rows.fix: Fry the paprika in a little oil for 30 seconds before adding the liquid next time. Use fresh paprika from a recently opened tin.

rows.symptom: The beef is still chewy after 8 hours
rows.cause: The slow cooker temperature may be lower than expected, or the pieces were cut too large.
rows.fix: Cook on HIGH for a further hour. The collagen in braising steak needs time and heat to convert to gelatin.

rows.cause: The vegetables released liquid during cooking, adding volume beyond what was expected.
rows.fix: Pour the sauce into a saucepan and reduce over medium-high heat until thickened, about 10 minutes. The beef can stay in the slow cooker on WARM.

rows.cause: The smoked paprika used may have been a hot variety rather than sweet-smoked.
rows.fix: Stir in a dollop of soured cream or a spoonful of plain yoghurt to cool the heat.

content.text: Goulash began as a Hungarian herders' dish, seasoned with dried paprika that could survive long journeys. It spread across Central Europe and arrived in British home cooking by the mid-20th century. The slow cooker version strips the technique down to its minimum: season, brown, assemble, wait. Serve with a cold glass of something and a piece of bread to clear the bowl.
